title: The number of key bits in AES does not change the packet width
summary: AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 all operate on 128-bit (16-byte) blocks.
applies: Byte representation and parameter explanation of cryptography questions
detail: The 128, 192, and 256 in the algorithm name refer to the number of key bits. Breaking the AES-256 ciphertext into 32-byte chunks merges adjacent chunks.
boundary: Grouping width cannot directly deduce the entire file length; mode, padding, and outer fields all affect storage length.
relevance: Avoid using the key length as the block length when checking ciphertext chunking, IV bytes, and file slicing.
